what: `attentionFor` builds the list of who notices a site being emptied by mapping `site.factionIds` through `this.repos.sects.getById`, which is seeded only from `SECTS` (`cultivation-support.ts:123`), so any claimant id belonging to `COURTS` or `APEX_INSTITUTIONS` is silently filtered out - taking the deed, the grudge and the player-facing line with it.
casesItMisses: `grave-shen-guyi` ("The Tended Tomb", occupantOrdinal 44) has `factionIds: ['court-third-sill']` and nothing else. A player who enters it and types "I take it" empties an ordinal-44 tomb tended by a court and gets: no `aDeedEntersTheWorld` fact (the `claimants.length > 0` guard fails), no `createGrudge` row, and not one sentence of attention - not even the `nameless` fallback, because `nameless` only counts claimants that survived the filter. The pitch would have banded 'unforgivable'. Same total silence for `trial-the-fourth-branch-station` ("The Counted Stair", `['apex-earth-vein-tower','court-kiln']`) and `trial-the-four-inward-faces` ("The Inward Faces", `['apex-long-cut','court-ninth-face']`); and `grave-yun-baiheng` ("The Stopped Ground", `['court-ninth-face','sect-clearwater-ward']`) loses half its claim. This is exactly the defect the block's own comment says it exists to close - "taking was strictly better than not taking, every time" - still live for four of the thirty sites.
generalShape: Resolve a claimant id the way `posture` in institution-verbs.ts already does - `this.repos.sects.getById(id) ?? getCourt(id) ?? getApexInstitution(id)` from `data/cultivation/hierarchy.ts` - so a house, a court and an apex are all bodies that can hold ground and hold a grudge about it. Nothing else in the block changes: the severity band, the deed and the discovery gate all read a name and an id.

what: `whatWouldItTake` (the `terms` / `a_trade` half of `request`) resolves what is being ASKED FOR through `resolvePill` and `theThingAskedFor(pillId)` only - `theThingAskedFor` opens with `PILLS.find(...)` and returns null for anything else - while `heldByTheirHouse` further filters `o.kind === 'pill'`.
casesItMisses: "ask Ru Yanzhi what she would take for The Hidden Edge" (an ordinary row in `data/cultivation/artifacts.ts`, power-rated, held on the standing register like every other object) is refused with "Nothing by that name that anybody trades. …Nothing in the world is called \"The Hidden Edge\" that a person would barter over." - a false sentence about the catalog. The same is true of every one of the twenty-four artifacts, the Heaven-Conversing Canon volumes, and any manual. Meanwhile the OTHER direction already prices all of them: `whatIsBeingPutDown` in what-a-holder-would-take-for-it.ts reads `ARTIFACTS.power`, `TECHNIQUES.grade` and `IMMORTAL_ITEMS` grade ceilings, and its own header argues at length that a rated blade must not fall through to the offerer's rung. So a player may OFFER The Hidden Edge at 45 and may not ASK for it at all.
generalShape: `theThingAskedFor` should ask the same question of every catalog `whatIsBeingPutDown` already asks it of - how high does it carry whoever ends up with it, off `power` / `grade` / the immortal ceiling - and return the same `TheThingAskedFor` shape, with `pastTheCashLine` read from the row's own tier rather than from `pillTradeTier` alone. `heldByTheirHouse` should match on the resolved row's id rather than on `kind === 'pill'`.

what: `standingToward` reads `entry.ambition?.blockedBy.includes(named.id)` in one direction only - from the asker's own house outward - and never asks whether the NAMED house's ambition is blocked by the asker's.
casesItMisses: `rivals` and `contestedWith` are perfectly symmetric across the catalog (measured: 0 one-way edges), so reading them one way is harmless. `blockedBy` is not, and is not meant to be: 39 of its edges are one-way. A disciple of the Azure Cloud Pavilion typing "where do we stand with the Azure Mist Court" gets "Nothing stands between Azure Cloud Pavilion and Azure Mist Court that anybody has written down, and nothing has been said either way" - while the Azure Mist Court's entire ambition ("The quarterly probation roll actually read by somebody at the terraces who could act on it") is `blockedBy: ['sect-azure-cloud-pavilion']`. Same silence for a Frostmirror Court member asking about the Orchid Court, whose ambition is "to be left where it is" and whose named obstacle is the Frostmirror Court. The single most actionable fact about the pair - you are the reason they cannot have what they want - is the one the read cannot say.
generalShape: Ask the catalog both ways at the same point: `getSect(named.id)?.ambition?.blockedBy.includes(position.sectId)` beside the existing clause, with its own sentence ("You are what stands between them and what they are after"). The two readings are different facts and the file already has the vocabulary for both.

what: `theReadThatAnswersIt` is a per-verb table of "the free read that answers a question about this act", and `craft` has no case in it, so a question about building falls to `default: { action: 'assess', target }`.
casesItMisses: "can I build a spirit boat?" matches `ASKING_RATHER_THAN_DOING` (`\bcan\s+i\b`), `craft` is in `TIME_CONSUMING_ACTIONS` and not in `READ_ONLY_ACTIONS`, so `costsTheAskerNothing` is false and the plan is rewritten to `{action:'assess', target:'spirit boat'}`. `GameService.assess` (turn-engine.ts:5838) then calls `handleAssess({against:'place', place:'spirit boat'})` - the player asking whether they can lay a keel gets an ambient-qi reading of a place called "spirit boat". The exact right free read already exists one call away: `planTheBuild` with nothing named returns `kind: 'listing'` - every bill, the rung gate on each, and what the pouch is short of - which `craft-verbs.ts` renders as a free action. The neighbouring `case 'refine'` returns `{action:'refine'}` for precisely this reason, in a comment that says so.
generalShape: Add `case 'craft': return { action: 'craft' };` beside `refine` - dropping the target reaches the bench listing exactly as dropping it reaches the cauldron listing. The table is the right shape; it went stale when `craft` was added to `ACTION_NAMES`.

what: `fold` declares the `FoldFix` as `'stood'` or refuses, reading only the knowledge table (`stageOf(...,'place',...) >= 'encountered'`). `FoldFix` has two members and the other one - `'seen'`, with its own `SEEN_FIX_ERROR` of 10% and its own branch in `landsShortByDays` - has no producer anywhere in `src/`.
casesItMisses: The `destinations` read this player just ran tells them, in `situated-reads.ts:617`, that "the far end has to be ground you have stood on **or something you have made out yourself**" - and in the same execution prints `whatCanBeSeenFromUpThere`, the ground a cultivator at ordinal 22 with `thousand-li-cloud-tread` can physically make out across the neighbouring provinces. A cultivator who has read Iron Ridge off a Span board (stage 'placed') and can see that ground from the air types "I fold to Iron Ridge" and is refused: "They know the name and not the place… what it needs is ground you have stood on." The engine models exactly this arrival - you land about a tenth of the road short, because a sighting is a worse fix than a footprint - and no sentence can reach it.
generalShape: Derive the fix from both channels the game already has rather than declaring it off one: `'stood'` where the knowledge stage reaches `encountered`, `'seen'` where `whatCanBeSeenFromUpThere` puts that ground inside this rung's horizon, null otherwise. `priceFold` already prices the difference and the refusal already has the right words for the remaining case.

what: `whatWasPutDownTheirThroat` picks the pill by counting the pouch - `carried.length === 1 ? carried[0] : null` - and never reads the name the player said, because `attack`'s signature carries no `rawInput` and no `topic` (turn-engine.ts:2805 passes only `action.intent` as `wanted`).
casesItMisses: A cultivator carrying a Lesser Healing Pill and a Soul-Hollowing Pill types "I force him to swallow the soul-hollowing pill". The sentence parses to `coerce` with intent `swallow` (verb-pattern-table.ts:1889), the fight ends in submission, and the answer is "You are carrying 2 different pills and did not say which one. <name> waits, which is the only thing left to them." - about a sentence that named it. The comment defends not GUESSING between a healing pill and a hollowing one, which is right; what is missing is reading the name, and the package has exactly one matcher for that already (`resolvePill`, and `whichThingTheyMeant` for the object case, both used by the theft path on the same turn shape).
generalShape: Carry the plan's `topic`/rawInput through `attack` onto `StandingFight` the way `wanted` already is, and resolve it against `listPouch` with `resolvePill` - falling back to the existing count rule when nothing was named. The one-pill shortcut then becomes the tail of the read rather than the whole of it.

what: `placeAChild` composes the child's id as the constant `child_of_${cultivator.id}`, commented as "the id the household tie already carries" - but `haveAChild` writes the tie under `child_${cultivator.id}_${party.id}_${today}` (match-verbs.ts:877), and `spendAWord` never checks that any such child exists.
casesItMisses: A player who has never used the `child` verb types "I ask Wei Lanya to place my child at the Azure Cloud Pavilion". `spendAWord` runs its house checks, passes, and returns a placement: a `serious` `sponsored_admission` favour is written to the obligation ledger, a defining `patron`/`client` tie is recorded, and the player is told "Placed, on a word to Wei Lanya. …The child is on sect-azure-cloud-pavilion's roll at the bottom of it." There is no child. And in the honest direction it fails too: a player who DID raise one has the tie indexed under `child_<me>_<them>_<day>` while the placement favour's `participants` names `child_of_<me>`, so the record that `spendAWord`'s own comment calls "the only route a placed child has back to their own story" points at an id no row carries.
generalShape: Read the child off the rows `haveAChild` wrote - the `child`-type relationship held by this cultivator - and refuse when there is none, the way `declineAMatch` reads the marriage pact off `openLedgerBetween` rather than off the sentence. The id then comes from the tie instead of from a second convention that nothing checks against the first.

what: `arriveAfterSpending` - the shared arrival for `ride`, `fold` and `passage` - runs `noteEncounter` and `noteWhoseGroundThisIs` but not `meetingYourOwnHouse` / `theStructureYouWereTold`, and returns no `perceived`, so none of the three callers can hand any to the turn. `move` (lines 302-331) does all four.
casesItMisses: A Frostmirror Court disciple who walks to the terraces arrives and is introduced to their own people standing there - `whatStandingAmongYourOwnShows` grants `named` on each, and `turn-engine.ts:1925` writes them. The same disciple who buys passage at a Span counter, folds, or rides a spirit boat to the same ground arrives and is introduced to nobody: the house that holds the ground is written (the shared helper does that half), the people of their own house are not. This is the "A Sword Elder who could not name one person in his own house" defect the `move` comment cites, still live on three of the four ways of arriving.
generalShape: Move the two `perceived` reads into `arriveAfterSpending` beside `noteWhoseGroundThisIs` and return them with `{skip, applied, world}`, so an arrival grants the same three facts however the ground was covered - and `move` becomes a caller of the shared helper rather than the only place the third fact lives.

what: The gate on the whole `sect` verb family is a hand-written five-word alternation `/\b(?:sect|order|school|clan|house|reserves?|treasur\w+|coffers)\b/`, and three more gates in the same function repeat it (line 3044 donate, line 3061 who-leads, line 3076 the house listing, line 610 ground-time) - none of them reads `A_HOUSE_TYPE_NOUN`, which this very file already imports at line 98 for one other veto.
casesItMisses: Measured through `dist/web/verb-pattern-table.js`. A member of Lantern Hall, Stone Marrow Hall or Nine Nether Hall typing `I resign from the hall` gets `unclear`; `I resign from the sect` gets `sect/leave`. `I leave the cult`, `I leave the court`, `I leave the grove` all get `unclear`, and `I leave the alliance` gets `interact/negotiate` - a plausible-looking answer to a resignation. `where do I stand in the pavilion` gets `status`, the character sheet, instead of `sect/standing`. `I donate to the hall` / `to the court` / `to the pavilion` -> `unclear`, while `I donate to the sect` works. `who is in charge of the court` -> `unclear`. `which courts take people` -> `unclear` and `tell me about the courts near here` -> `investigate("courts near here")`, while `which houses take people` and `tell me about the sects near here` both reach `sect` - and the comment directly above line 3076 says the missing plural `houses` was itself the bug that was fixed there once. The catalog has seven Courts, three Halls, three Pavilions, two Temples, one Cult, one Alliance, one Grove.
generalShape: Drop the hand alternations and use `A_HOUSE_TYPE_NOUN_OR_PLURAL` from `./what-a-house-is-called.js`, which is the one list `tests/data/the-nouns-a-house-ends-with.test.ts` ratchets against `SECTS`. That test only checks the list against the catalog, not that callers use it, which is why exactly one call site in the whole tree (line 566) actually does.

what: `AN_INSTITUTION_IS_BEING_ASKED` decides whether the thing named in the sentence is a BODY rather than a person, off a hand list of nine words (`sects?|houses?|clans?|orders?|schools?|halls?|courts?|pavilions?|councils?|elders?`) - the catalog's houses end in 27 different type nouns. It gates both the petition asking-verbs branch (line 460) and the ending-a-house branch (line 332).
casesItMisses: `I ask the Azure Dew Sect for a manual` -> `petition/grant`, correctly. `I ask the Clear River Alliance for a manual`, `I ask the Burnt Earth Temple for a manual`, `I ask the Bone Lantern Cult for a manual` and `I ask the Ancient Bough Grove for a manual` all -> `request/a_thing` - routed to the ask-a-PERSON resolver, which is the exact inversion the comment at line 458 says the noun gate exists to prevent, running in the other direction. And the ending branch: this file's own comment says *"Measured before this: 'I end the Hollow Court' reached the seduction verb, because the house is called a Court"* - `Court` was added, so `I end the Hollow Court` now works, while `I end the Bone Lantern Cult` and `I disband the Burnt Earth Temple` -> `unclear`, and `I destroy the Clear River Alliance` -> `interact/negotiate`, a conversation with a house the player meant to end.
generalShape: Build the alternation from `A_HOUSE_TYPE_NOUN_OR_PLURAL` in `what-a-house-is-called.ts` plus the non-name phrases already here (`the seat`, `my house`, `patriarch`, `hall master`…). This file already generates `IMMORTAL_ITEM_NAMED` from `IMMORTAL_ITEMS` at line 57, so the derive-from-catalog shape is four lines above the hand list.

what: Four more hand-written house-word alternations in this file - `SECT_CURRICULUM_NOUNS` (295), the summons row (77), `CLAIMING_THE_HOUSES_AUTHORITY` (131) and the house-property taking gate (366) - each spelling out `sect|house|clan|school|order` and no more, so a member refers to their own body by a word the file has never heard of.
casesItMisses: `what does my sect teach` -> `sect/curriculum`. `what does my hall teach`, `what does my court teach`, `what does my cult teach`, `what does my pavilion teach` -> all `unclear`, for members of Lantern Hall, Orchid Court, Bone Lantern Cult and Azure Cloud Pavilion. Worse on the summons row: `what does the sect want of me` -> `sect/summons`, but `what does the cult want of me` and `what does the hall want of me` -> `request/wants` with `target: "cult"` / `"hall"` - the engine goes looking for a person by that name, which is a confident wrong answer rather than a refusal, on the one read that tells a player what saying no to their house would cost.
generalShape: Same fix as the other two: `A_HOUSE_TYPE_NOUN_OR_PLURAL` from `what-a-house-is-called.ts`. Its header claims "ONE LIST, BECAUSE THERE WERE TEN" and names `sect-phrasings.ts` as one of the ten; measured, only `verb-pattern-table.ts:566` was ever converted.

what: `RANKS` is a nine-word set (`elder, disciple, master, warden, head, patriarch, servant, guard, attendant`) matched against `sectRank`, and nothing checks it against `SECTS[].ranks`, which is where every rank title in the world actually lives.
casesItMisses: `matriarch` is absent while `patriarch` is present, and the head of Orchid Court is titled `Orchid Matriarch`: standing in front of her, `I speak to the matriarch` returns null from `theDescriptionThisIs`, falls through to the name resolver, and is answered *"does not know the name, and asks who that is"* - precisely the failure `whatTheDescriptionAskedFor` was written to stop ("A description is not got wrong"). Same for `the abbot` (Burnt Earth Temple's head), `the monk` (Temple Monk / Inner Monk), `the physician` (three of Verdant Spring Valley's seven rungs), `the alchemist` (Cinnabar Crucible Sect), `the smith`, `the ascetic`, `the keeper`, `the factor`, `the steward`, `the envoy`, `the sovereign`, `the chief`. Counted over the catalog: 113 of 227 rungs (50%) and 24 of 35 house heads cannot be named by any word this set knows, and two houses - Thousand Treasure Pavilion and The Severed - have no reachable rung at all. The same set also builds the pool in `theWordsThisPersonAnswersTo`, so a reader is never offered those people's rank as a way of naming them either. The design owner's quoted line on this feature is *"people call people by title a lot in xianxia, not just by name"*.
generalShape: Harvest the head words from `SECTS[].ranks` - split each title on non-letters and keep the nouns - the way this package already harvests `TRADE_PHRASES` from `OCCUPATIONS` and `DUTY_PHRASES` from `SUMMONS_ENTRIES`/`COMMISSION_ENTRIES` in `verb-pattern-table.ts:1045-1125`, with a ratchet test like `the-nouns-a-house-ends-with.test.ts`. The two sibling lists - `A_RANK_IN_THE_PLURAL` in `acts-over-a-set.ts:151` and `POINTING_AT_A_RANK` in `turn-engine.ts:957` - are third and fourth copies of the same question and disagree with each other today (the comment at `acts-over-a-set.ts:136` says it "Matches POINTING_AT_A_RANK"; it carries three words that one does not).

what: `A_LEANING_IN_THE_PLURAL` requires the set phrase to end in one of `sects?|houses?|clans?|orders?|schools?|cultivators?|disciples?|people|ones?`, so a leaning said with any other house noun is not recognised as a leaning and falls through to `A_WHOLE_HOUSE`, which reads it as one house with that name.
casesItMisses: `I kill all the demonic sects` -> `of_alignment('demonic')`, the six demonic houses, exactly as the design owner's quoted sentence asks. `I kill all the demonic cults` -> `members_of` a house called "demonic cults", which `factionMeant` resolves to nothing, so `actOverASet` refuses it: *"Unresolved set ... nothing this cultivator can name answers to it."* The world's demonic houses include the Bone Lantern **Cult**, Burnt Earth **Temple** and Crimson Abyss **Fortress**, and "the demonic cults" is the plainest way anybody says it in this genre. `every demonic temple` and `all the righteous temples` fail the same way. The file's own header says "A branch that fires for families and not for other sets is wrong, so the recognition is over the SHAPE of the phrase" - and this is the one shape whose recognition is over a word list instead.
generalShape: Make the trailing noun group `A_HOUSE_TYPE_NOUN_OR_PLURAL` plus the people words already there. The neighbouring `A_WHOLE_HOUSE` (line 132) carries a seventh copy of the same eight-word list and is inconsistent because of it: `all of the Azure Dew Sect` yields house "Azure Dew" with the type noun stripped, `all of the Bone Lantern Cult` yields "Bone Lantern Cult" with it left on.

what: `A_PORTABLE_THING` is a hand-written list of ~30 object nouns that decides, for every taking and every theft, whether a phrase names a thing or a person - and it is not checked against `src/data/cultivation/artifacts.ts`, which is the world's object table.
casesItMisses: Of the 23 rows in `artifacts.ts`, only two head nouns are on the list (`sabre`, `stone`). Measured: `I take the notched sabre` -> `interact/take, topic: "notched sabre"`. `I take the Hollow Bell`, `I take the Closed Fan`, `I take the Thunder-Struck Rod`, `I take the Black Ice Key`, `I take the Cinnabar Brush` -> all `unclear`. `I take the sword off him` -> `interact/steal`; `I take the bell off him` -> `unclear`. And the person-vs-thing half fails the way the README already documents for boats: `I steal Wei Lanya's sword` correctly gives `target: "Wei Lanya", topic: "Wei Lanya's sword"`, while `I steal Wei Lanya's fan` gives `target: "Wei Lanya's fan"` - a theft aimed at a person by that name, which is byte-for-byte the `I steal the spirit boat from Cao Nuolin` defect the comment inside this constant says was fixed by adding hulls and carriages to it by hand. It broke again for the next noun because the fix was a word, not a source.
generalShape: Generate the alternation from the catalogs the objects actually come from - `ARTIFACTS`, `PILLS`, the manual catalog - the way `institution-phrasings.ts:57` builds `IMMORTAL_ITEM_NAMED` from `IMMORTAL_ITEMS`, and the way `TRADE_PHRASES` and `DUTY_PHRASES` are built one screen below this constant in the same file.

what: `markDead` closes the attached run for ANY cultivator carrying a `runId`, with no check that the dead person is the run's own cultivator - while `advanceRealm`, forty lines above in the same class, gates the identical write on `c.kind === 'pc'` and explains at length why it has to.
casesItMisses: `ADMIN spawn_encounter ordinal=5` creates the opponent with `runId: run.id` and `kind: 'enemy'` (admin-manage.ts:1107-1110). The operator then calls `combat_manage({action:'resolve', opponent:{cultivatorId:'<that id>'}})`, the player wins, and combat-manage.ts:725 calls `repos.cultivators.markDead(opponentRow.id, 'combat_defeat', ...)`. That runs `UPDATE runs SET status='dead', death_cause='combat_defeat' WHERE id=<the PLAYER'S run> AND status='active'`. The player is alive at full HP and their run is closed; every subsequent tool call falls into `resolveActiveRun`'s `run_ended` branch (cultivation-support.ts:205) and answers "Death is permanent; a finished run is never reopened." The comment in `advanceRealm` already names this exact NPC ("`admin_manage.spawn_encounter` builds its opponent with the player's `runId`") and says "the same road is taken by every NPC the world advances inside a run" - it fixed the peak stamp and left the death write.
generalShape: The run row already knows whose life it is: `runs.cultivator_id`, which the storage README calls out as the enforced side of the circular key. The `UPDATE` should carry `AND cultivator_id = @cultivatorId`, or take the same `c.kind === 'pc'` gate `advanceRealm` uses two methods above, so the guard is a property of the run's ownership rather than a line one of the two writers remembered.

what: `set_curriculum` writes the decreed shelf to `view.ledger.teaches`, a per-cultivator flag that nothing outside `loadHouse` in this same file ever reads - while `set_admission` in the same handler family writes its decree through to the world's `sects` row via `repos.sects.upsert`.
casesItMisses: A player who is head of the Azure Dew Sect (`sects.ts:909`, `teaches: ['azure-dew-gathering-canon','foundation-tempering-scripture']`) runs `sect_manage({action:'set_curriculum', teach:['<a taught-provenance art>']})`. The handler charges standing through `curriculumChangeCost`/`resolveAct`, can lose elders, lose disciples, trigger a head challenge or lose the house outright, and returns `decreed: true` with `teachesNow` carrying the new art. The player then runs `technique_manage({action:'learn', techniqueId:'<that art>'})` and technique-manage.ts:415-416 reads `getSect(cultivator.sectId).teaches` - the static catalog - and refuses with `no_road_to_this_book`: "Azure Dew Sect does not teach it." `getSectsTeaching` (technique-manage.ts:434, 496) is the catalog too, so the refusal's own housesTeachingIt count is unchanged as well. Retiring the house's signature art has the mirror failure: `signatureRetired: true` comes back and members can still learn it. The player has paid a generational price for a decree with no reader.
generalShape: There is already one composed answer to "what does this house teach": `loadHouse`'s `teaches: ledger.teaches ?? facts?.teaches ?? []` (sect-leadership.ts:291). Either `handleLearn` and `getSectsTeaching` should ask that composition instead of `getSect(...).teaches`, or `set_curriculum` should write the decreed shelf back onto the `sects` row the way `loadHouse` already writes `admissionOrdinal` and `powerOrdinal` through `repos.sects.upsert` (sect-leadership.ts:268-274) so every existing reader sees it unchanged.

what: `read_hazard` re-derives a hazard's source row from a hand-written prefix table (`creature_`, `room_`) that is never checked against `scanHazards`, the function that mints the ids and produces four shapes.
casesItMisses: `engine/perception/hazard-detector.ts` mints `room_<id>_atmos_<a>` (line 79), `creature_<id>` (102), `combatant_<tokenId>` (131) and `narrative_<noteId>_<tag>` (162). `perception_manage({action:'list_hazards', targetRef:{kind:'encounter', encounterId:'<enc>'}})` lists every hostile token as `combatant_<id>`; passing any one of those straight back as `perception_manage({action:'read_hazard', hazardId:'combatant_<id>'})` debits 1 attentional_capacity at line 505 and then falls out of both prefix branches, returning `disposition:'unknown', reason:'hazard_not_resolvable_from_id'`. The same happens for every `narrative_<noteId>_hazard:<tag>` id a `scene` target lists. Two of the three target kinds the tool accepts can list hazards that the tool's own deep read cannot resolve, and the observer is charged for the miss.
generalShape: The id minter is the catalog of id shapes. `handleReadHazard` should resolve the hazard by running `scanHazards` over the target it belongs to and matching `hazard.id`, the way `handleListHazards` and `handleAssess` already do, instead of keeping a second, shorter list of what an id can look like.

what: `handleMarket` filters `PRICES` by `args.category` alone and never by `standing.settlementKind`, so every settlement in the world sells the whole 41-line board plus the full manual stall - while `handleWork` in the same file gates every occupation on exactly that field.
casesItMisses: Standing in Clear Creek Village (`regions/low-fall.ts:167`, `kind: 'village'`, in the home region), `market` prints the Lesser Healing Pill, the Qi-Gathering Pill, the Clear Meridian Pill, the Marrow-Washing Pill and `manualsAStallCarries()` in full - in a place whose own catalog row says `lacks: ['pills of any grade', 'a manual of any kind', ...]` (mortal-world.ts SETTLEMENTS). Six Li (`regions/quiet-marches.ts:193`, `kind: 'hamlet'`) sells the same board while its row says `lacks: ['any medicine at all', 'anyone who can read']`. In the same file three hundred lines up, `work` correctly refuses `job-scribe` in a hamlet with "Nobody in Six Li is hiring for Scribe. What is going here: ..." - so the settlement gate exists, is populated, and reaches labour but not goods. A waystation or site place resolves `settlementKind` to null (where-a-cultivator-is-standing.ts:25) and so escapes the work gate too: standing at Halfway Gate, a shed on a road, `work` offers `job-outer-chores` (sect_town only) and `job-house-guest` (city only).
generalShape: `Occupation.settlements` already carries the shape - where a thing exists, as a list of settlement kinds - and `standingOf(cultivator).settlementKind` is already resolved and already the gate `handleWork` runs. `Price` should carry the same column and `handleMarket` should apply the same filter, and `standingOf` should distinguish "a place the gazetteer names that is not a settlement" from "a place we could not find" rather than folding both to null.

what: `grant_knowledge` can lift the awareness gate over two of the four `KnownEntityKind` registers - `place` and `sect` - and there is no action anywhere on the ADMIN surface that reveals a PERSON the world already holds; the only route to a nameable person is `spawn_encounter`, which authors a new one.
casesItMisses: `members.ts` holds 186 named people who are seeded into the world by `seedNamedFigures`, and `interact`, `request`, `attack` and `propose` all resolve their target through `KnowledgeGate.isAwareOf(id, 'cultivator', ...)`. An operator who wants to play "I ask Han Peiru to teach me the flying blade" - a real Azure Cloud Pavilion member standing on its own ground - has `grant_knowledge kind=sect` (grants the house, not the person), `grant_knowledge kind=place`, and nothing else; the file's own `THE_ACTIONS_THAT_ARRANGE_IT['engine.resolveParty']` (forcing-an-attempt-to-land.ts:87) answers that refusal with `ADMIN spawn_encounter`, whose registered description is "CREATES A PERSON" with a `randomUUID` and a name string. So the one register that four verbs resolve against can only be reached by authoring a stranger, in a surface whose every other action says "ADMIN reveals what exists; it does not author." `readAdminSentence`'s knowledge subject even accepts the word `names` (admin-said-as-a-sentence.ts:92) and maps it to no register, so "grant me the names of everyone here" silently grants places and houses and no people.
generalShape: The person register already exists and is already written the right way: `spawn_encounter` calls `knowledge.learnIfNew({kind:'cultivator', ...})` at admin-manage.ts:1132 after minting its row. `grant_knowledge` should carry `cultivator` as a third kind and draw its entries from `repos.cultivators.roster()` (which `handleRoster` already lists) or `MEMBERS`, exactly as it draws places from `REGIONS` plus the live world's locations and houses from `SECTS` - a reveal rather than a create.

what: `sentenceFor` is a hand-written `switch (s.kind)` carrying 17 sentences against the 42-member `HistoricalEventKind` union in `history.ts`, and every kind it has not been taught silently falls to `${who} did something${at} that people are still repeating` - a sentence that drops the house, the topic and everything the fact actually carries.
casesItMisses: A player standing in a square types `I declare war on the Ashen Forge Clan`, the act is refused, and `theWorldHeardYouSayIt` (turn-engine.ts:2622) files a `said_in_public` fact with `factionIds: [ashen-forge]`, `data.saidAbout: 'Ashen Forge Clan'` and `data.wouldHave: 'attack'`. `said_in_public` has no case, so every teller in the world repeats it as "Wei Lanya did something at Clear River Ford that people are still repeating, this season, and nobody thinks much of it." The house it was about is never in the sentence - while `bend` still writes a knowledge record for that house into `named`, so the player is handed a record for a house whose name they were never told. The turn-engine comment above that call says in full that the point of the fact is that it "arrives at the named house as *some lunatic has declared war on us*"; it cannot, because the only branch that would print `house` is one of the seventeen. The same hole swallows `territory_changed`, which is the commonest institutional event the pressure table fires (`border_moved`, line 2845 of the-world-changing-on-its-own.ts): a vein changing hands between two named houses, with `factionIds: [previous, claimant]` and no actors, is repeated as "somebody did something at the Nine Hundred Paces that people are still repeating." Also unreachable: `injury`, `presumed_dead`, `gave_up_waiting`, `promotion`, `grant_renewed`, `migration`, `oath_sworn`, `resource_contested`.
generalShape: Compose the sentence from what the fact carries rather than from a list of kinds it has been taught: the fact already holds `actors` with roles, `factionIds`, `place`, `magnitude` and its own authored name-free line in `data.unattributed`, and `digest.ts` already proves the safe shape one layer over - `FALLBACK` there is a `Partial<Record<HistoricalEventKind, string>>` whose fallback is explicitly argued for and whose entries include `said_in_public`. Either make this table the same total `Record<HistoricalEventKind, ...>` the repo prefers so a new kind does not compile until somebody has said how it is repeated, or drop the switch and build the clause from the roles on `actors` plus `house` - a doer, a done-to, a house, a place - which is what `bend` already hands it.

what: `enshrineRun`'s remembrance block finds who remembers the dead by `n.factionId === faction.id` and takes the first six in roster order, then `upsertRelationship`s an `acquaintance` tie over whatever those people already held - so the world's record of a death is keyed on shared membership rather than on who actually had a tie to the person, and it overwrites the ties it lands on.
casesItMisses: `enshrineRun` is the ONLY death path a player takes - `settleWhatTheyWereCarrying` in web/estate-settlement.ts:286 calls it and never calls `settleNpcDeath`. Two live cases. (1) A housemate who holds an enemy tie to the player at -0.55, written by `whatTheConfrontationDidToThem` (what-a-confrontation-does-to-somebody-the-world-holds.ts:272) the day the player beat them in a duel, is one of the first six rows of that house: `upsertRelationship` replaces `kind` and `standing` wholesale, so the person who hated the player most now holds them at `acquaintance`, +0.3, note "Was there when it cost the sect something." That is exactly the defect this repo's own README (engine/world/README.md:1311) records finding and fixing in `settleNpcDeath` - "A son inherited his own mother as an acquaintance of his father's" - and `settleNpcDeath` now guards it with `if (state.npcs[at].relationships.some(r => r.targetId === account.targetId)) continue;`. `enshrineRun` never got the guard. (2) A player who never joined a house - an ordinary way to play, and the case `standing.ts` writes a whole separate refusal for - dies with a master taught through `request`/`handleLearn` and four allies the yearly ties pass wrote onto their roster row, and `deceased.factionId` is null, so the entire block is skipped: `rememberedBy` is empty, no memory is stored, no `recordMasterLost` fires for anybody they were teaching, and nobody in the world remembers them at all.
generalShape: Read `deceased.relationships` - the ties the dead person actually held, which the world has been writing onto that row all run - instead of `state.npcs.filter(n => n.factionId === ...)`. `settleNpcDeath` in time.ts:609 is the same act already generalised and is the module to defer to: it walks the deceased's own ties, is symmetric on `GRUDGE_STANDING`/`FRIENDSHIP_STANDING` from gatherings.ts rather than on a bare `-0.4` (legacy.ts:363 still has the bare literal and still inherits only the enemies), skips a target the heir already has a view of, and calls `recordMasterLost` for every `disciple` tie regardless of house. Either route the player's death through it or make `enshrineRun` read the same three things.

what: `CARRIAGES_BY_GRADE` and `A_CARRIAGE_COSTS` are hand-written lists of three conveyance ids that stand in for "what a house keeps in the yard", and neither is checked against `CONVEYANCES` in `data/cultivation/what-a-house-moves-its-people-on.ts` - which carries eight rows, marks each one `holding: 'none' | 'personal' | 'counted' | 'tracked'`, and has `countedHolding` return 0 for anything that is not `counted`.
casesItMisses: `conv-carriage-heaven` is `holding: 'tracked'`, so `countedHolding(faction.resources, 'conv-carriage-heaven')` is 0 by construction, forever. Two consequences, both live. (1) At line 1655 the yard is computed with `countedHolding` and at 1660 a house with a purse over 40,000 stones is the first `find` hit: it pays 40,000 through `adjustCountedHolding`, which writes a `conveyance:conv-carriage-heaven` line that `countedHolding`, `countedConveyancesHeld` and `describeCountedHoldings` all refuse to read. The yard is still empty next year, so it pays again - and this branch runs before the `SENDINGS_PER_HOUSE_YEAR` gate, i.e. every faction every year. With `applyFactionEconomy` giving a two-vein house 10,000 a year, the richest houses in the world are precisely the ones that burn their treasury on a carriage nothing can see, and only houses that fall into the 8,000-39,999 band ever get a conveyance that works. (2) At line 1699 the conveyance handed to `postingFor` is drawn from the same three ids through the same predicate, so a house that has just launched a spirit boat or a named carriage out of `applyConveyanceBuilding` - 150 lines further down the same file, which correctly asks `conveyanceKeptAs(recipe.grade)` and pushes a real `ObjectRecord` into `state.objects` - sends its next party on foot, and every party after that, forever. The two counted mounts (`conv-mount-mortal`, `conv-mount-earth`) are invisible to both halves too, so the catalog's "the reason a house with nothing still has something" reaches no sending.
generalShape: Ask the catalog. `CONVEYANCES.filter(c => c.holding === 'counted')` is the yard and `countedConveyancesHeld(faction.resources)` already returns it sorted-by-nothing with counts; the tracked half is `state.objects.filter(o => o.ownerId === faction.id && o.data.conveyanceId)`, which is exactly what `craftOwnedBy` does for the catalog's own five craft. `conveyanceKeptAs` is named in this file as "the single authority and every caller asks it rather than deciding separately" - `applyConveyanceBuilding` asks it and `applySendings` does not. Price should come off the catalog row (grade/range/heads) rather than a three-entry map keyed on ids, so adding a ninth conveyance does not silently acquire a price of undefined.

what: `advanceWorldForPlay` defines what happened in the span as `state.history.facts.slice(factsBefore)` - newly appended ROWS - so a fact the ledger folds into an existing row instead of appending is not in `events`, is not in the digest, and reaches the player nowhere.
casesItMisses: `appendWorldFact` merges by default, and `recurrenceKeyOf` excludes only `day` and the four recurrence keys - so a repeating scheduled effect, whose summary and `data.scheduledEffectId` are byte-identical every firing, appends exactly once in the life of a world. `seedGrantSchedule` (seeding.ts:1706) puts one on the books for every federated house: "The Ashen Forge Clan's grant on its vein comes up for renewal", `visibility: 'faction'`, which is the sect channel `sectThreshold` exists to serve. It fired 167 times in the measured two-thousand-year world. A player who joins that house in year 1200 and secludes through three renewals is told about none of them, because the row carrying all three is dated whenever it first fired and is not in the slice. The same swallows every repeating `market_shift`, `assessment` and `meeting` whose statement does not change. The read side was clearly meant to handle it and cannot see it: `DigestLine.occurrences` and `collapseRepeats` in digest.ts exist to fold repeats at render time, and `occurrencesOf`, `lastOccurrenceOf` and `describeWithRecurrence` are exported from a-fact-that-keeps-happening-is-one-row.ts with no reader anywhere in src/.
generalShape: The span's events are the facts that OCCURRED in it, not the rows that were created in it. `appendWorldFact` already knows which of the two it did and returns the row either way; have it (or the driver) collect the rows touched in the span, and let the digest read `lastOccurrenceOf(fact)` for the date and `occurrencesOf(fact)` for `DigestLine.occurrences` rather than `fact.day` and 1. Everything needed is written and exported; nothing reads it.

what: `ruinProvenance` writes `builderName: ruin.name` - the ruin's own place name - into the field `identifyBuilder` hands back as the name of the house that built it, while the builder's real name sits on the `faction_fallen` fact's `data.factionName` and in `prior.deadFactionNames`.
casesItMisses: `seedPriorAges` draws `ruin.name` from `RUIN_NAMES` (history.ts:1203) - a place name like Cold Spring - and puts the dead house's name, `factionName(srng)`, on the fall fact at history.ts:1144. So for the ancient sealed ruins, which are every ruin a world opens holding and the ones the whole "depth, not scale" design is about, a player who reaches `provenanceReadOrdinal` on a `documented` site gets `placed: true` and `builderName: 'Cold Spring'` - Cold Spring was built by Cold Spring. `provenance.ts` renders that as the answer to "whose was this", and the reading is gated behind a comprehension key precisely so it feels earned. The same field is written correctly twelve hundred lines away by `ruinFromFallenSeat` (provenance.ts:897, `builderName: input.houseName`), which is the ruin the LIVE world makes when a house falls - so two ruins standing in one province answer the identical read two different ways, and the older one, which is the one worth digging, is the wrong one.
generalShape: Carry the dead house's name on the `Ruin` descriptor the way `Scar` already carries `failedName` and `Crossing` carries `crossedName`, and have `ruinProvenance` write that - the seeder has it in scope as `name` on the very line it sets `formerFactionId`, and `PriorAges.deadFactionNames` is already collecting it for somebody else. `builderId` is already the faction id, so the pair should resolve to one body; `nameOfBody` in ruin-gatekeepers.ts is the existing id-to-name read for exactly this.

what: howFarTheyWouldGo switches on a SectAlignment the CALLER declares, and both callers declare it from whichever house the wronged party happens to be on the roll of (asking-verbs.ts:452 `theirSect?.alignment ?? null`, combat-verbs.ts:1338 `getSect(factionId)?.alignment`), so how far a PERSON will go about being wronged is decided by their robe rather than by anything they have ever done.
casesItMisses: A rogue with a killing on the ledger. theAccountsAFightOpens writes an `unforgivable` grudge naming the killer, and whatTheirRecordMakesThem reads that as `demonic` at WHAT_MAKES_IT_A_METHOD = 2 - entities.ts:330 already prints 'Their own record reads demonic' about him to the player's face. Now threaten him in public and land it: weighTheWrong = 1 base + 1 force + 1 landed + 1 public = 4; his factionId is null so the branch taken is `neutral`, which returns 'injured', while the demonic row returns 'killed' at weight >= 4. The directory README's own measurement is 39 people on the ledger as killers of whom 20 read demonic; every one of those on no roll, or on a righteous roll, is resolved off the wrong row. The mirror is equally live: an empty-ledger Skin-rank outer disciple of a demonic house answers a landed public robbery (weight 5) with 'killed' where neutral gives 'crippled'.
generalShape: Derive it rather than declare it. personal-alignment.ts sits in the same directory and returns the same three-word SectAlignment off the obligation rows (whatTheirRecordMakesThem), and personal-record.ts already assembles exactly that call for any id including an NPC. Read the person's derived alignment, falling back to the house's field only where WhatSomebodyIs.nothingEitherWay is true - which is also the only reading under which 'by default its rogue neutral' is a statement about a person instead of a statement about a missing column.

what: grudgeAgainstYou (and owedYourWay directly above it) count only rows whose holderId is the subject in person, so every account held by the HOUSE the subject answers to weighs zero in oddsOf - even though Party.factionId is on the very input being read.
casesItMisses: Kill a ranked member of a house in a fight. theAccountsAFightOpens (going-further-than-an-agreed-bout-allowed.ts:352-361) writes a grave or unforgivable row with holderId = that house's id and subjectId = the player, and combat-verbs.ts:1823 persists it. Then ask any other member of that house for a courtesy: oddsOf returns grudge: 0, the mechanical channel prints no grudge term at all, and the odds are byte-identical to a stranger's. This directory's README calls that row 'now between institutions' and measured 202 of them off 111 deeds over three hundred years; nothing on the asking side has ever read one. The caller compounds it - asking-verbs.ts:359 passes openLedgerBetween(player, party), whose SQL is filtered to the two ids, so even a widened predicate would be handed nothing to widen over.
generalShape: The subject's side of the ledger is the subject plus whatever answers for them. Count rows where holderId is the subject OR the subject's factionId (already on Party), and have the caller hand in the rows standing against the actor rather than only the pair rows - the same widening what-a-deed-leaves.ts performs when it sets houseIsAParty and files the institutional row.

what: whatTheWrongedPartyDid re-derives the wrong from WRONG_BEHIND_INTENT[intent] and returns [] when that table has no row, so the entire reprisal layer is keyed on the word the parser picked - and it discards the `wrong` that howItLandedOn already computed twenty lines earlier at asking-verbs.ts:407.
casesItMisses: Two live cases pointing opposite ways. (a) Say anything with a non-wrong intent to somebody whose brother you killed: howItLandedOn returns 'threatened' via the `owed`/`feeling` ground in how-they-took-what-you-said.ts:174, that value is written onto the ledger marks and the facts, and then whatTheWrongedPartyDid looks up WRONG_BEHIND_INTENT['persuade'], finds nothing and returns [] - the module's headline case, 'a pleasantry from somebody who buried your brother is not a pleasantry', leaves a record and no reprisal. (b) That table is also the only door into whatTheyDoAboutBeingWronged and it reaches four of the eight members of `Wrong`; grep confirms no caller anywhere passes a woundKey. So `wounded`, `violated`, `interfered_with_a_crossing` and `killed` are unreachable, and with them the whole spentThemselves branch: wouldTheySpendThemselves requires !canBeGivenBack, which no reachable wrong has, so WHAT_SPENDING_EVERYTHING_REACHES and its 'PINNED BY TEST' calibration cannot fire in play. Cripple somebody permanently in an agreed duel and the one person that branch was written for - who can never be made whole and cannot reach you - does nothing at all.
generalShape: Pass the wrong that was already decided. howItLandedOn returns the act as the person on the receiving end was in a position to take it; whatTheWrongedPartyDid should take that Wrong plus the woundKey when a wound was actually dealt, and the combat and site paths that mint permanent wounds should hand the same value in - so what somebody answers is a property of what was done to them rather than of which row of a verb table the parser landed on.

what: theyHaveSomethingToAnswerFor is documented as 'open records where THIS hearer is the subject and the injured party is what the words named - their house, their dead, their ground', but its only caller computes it from ledgerAbout(cultivator.id) (turn-engine.ts:11158), a query that returns only rows naming the PLAYER, so the injured party can only ever be the player in person.
casesItMisses: The example this file and AGENTS.md both open with. A war between houses writes grudges held by a house against the people who killed its members. Join that house, stand in front of the man who killed three of its disciples, and say anything: `owed` is false because he never wronged you personally and `feeling` is nothing_either_way, so howTheyTookIt returns took: null with 'there is nothing between these two for it to land on', and he hears an introduction. Identical for the man who killed your sect-brother - the sect holds that row and you do not, so the read is blank and nothing follows.
generalShape: The question is whether an open account stands against this hearer held by anything the words named. Query the other end of the ledger (obligations where subject_id = them.id, which ObligationLedger.against already exposes) and intersect the holders with the parties the phrase actually reached - the player, the player's factionId, the player's kin, the house whoHeardTheirNameIn already resolved - instead of intersecting with the player's own two-column ledger read.

what: The pairwise feeling read discards every row whose holder is not the person themselves, so an account held by the house they answer to contributes nothing, and there is no parameter through which a caller could say which house that is.
casesItMisses: Kill a ranked member of a house in front of its people. The dead man's brother holds his own kin row (what-a-deed-leaves.ts writes one per relative at the same weight) and reads `despondent`. The four house-mates standing beside him hold nothing personally, because that account was filed on the house - so whatTheyFeelAboutYou returns nothing_either_way for each of them, howTheyCarryIt returns null, and scene-person-readings.ts puts not one word about any of them in the prose while their house carries a grave grudge naming the player. The scene layer already knows which of them share the victim's sectId - it counts them for the room line - but the feeling read, which is what actually produces a person's bearing, cannot be told.
generalShape: Take the subject's houseId alongside theirId and count rows held by either, exactly as the ledger writes them. what-a-deed-leaves.ts deliberately files the institutional row on the house, so a reader that accepts only a person id can never see the half of the ledger that module exists to open.

what: ROOT_FOUNDATION_SCORE is a hand-written `Record<string, number>` listing four spirit-root grades (single, mutated, dual, muddled) when SpiritRootGrade in spirit-roots.ts has six - `triple` and `quad` are missing, and the `string` key type means the compiler never notices.
casesItMisses: A cultivator with the Metal-Wood-Earth Triple Root (weight 99/999) or the Metal-Wood-Earth-Water Quad Root (weight 117/999) - together 21.6% of every root ever rolled - reaches the 12->13 crossing. assessFoundation pushes `delta: ROOT_FOUNDATION_SCORE['triple']` = undefined, the reduce produces `score = NaN`, every `score >= t.min` in FOUNDATION_THRESHOLDS is false, and the `?? 'damaged'` fallback fires. So one cultivator in five lays a `damaged` foundation (×0.55 rate, −0.12 breakthrough, +0.06 toll, 'no pill treats it') no matter how they prepared - dense qi, a foundation pill, clean meridians, unhurried, all of it discarded - and the narration hint reads 'score NaN'. The tests never see it because tests/engine/cultivation/fixtures.ts defaults spiritRoot to 'single_fire'.
generalShape: Key it `Record<SpiritRootGrade, number>` so the compiler forces every grade in SPIRIT_ROOTS to be priced, the same shape FOUNDATION_AMBIENT_SCORE and FOUNDATION_EFFECTS already use in this file.

what: `traditionOrDefault(combatant.traditionId)` reads a tradition the CALLER declares on CombatantInput, when the world already holds which road is walked where - Region.traditionId in region-schema.ts, and the house someone belongs to - and no code path in play ever fills the field.
casesItMisses: The whole Silent Cliffs (THE_QUIET_MARCHES, `traditionId: 'tradition-cut'`) is carvers, and named figures like Third Face Ren (ordinal 19, guest elder at the Stone Marrow Hall) and the woman at Six Li (ordinal 26) are carvers standing inside the Jade Gorge. A player fights one: src/web/combat-verbs.ts builds the opponent spec with no traditionId, combat-manage's combatantFromOpponent passes `spec.traditionId` = undefined, and traditionOrDefault falls back to 'tradition-drawn'. So the opponent gets a soul factor they do not have, loses the +0.15 body line, is weakened by thin ambient qi a carver does not draw on, and - the one that matters - resolveExchange's `soulAttacksAffect(defender.tradition)` returns true, so the soul-strike nullification and its authored line ('the single most dangerous fact about the Cut Road and the one outsiders discover last') can never fire in a played fight. killRequirement likewise tells the winner the body was enough when the world says the seam has to be quarried out and scattered. Region.traditionId is declared in the schema and read by nothing anywhere in src/.
generalShape: Derive the tradition where the combatant is built - read it off the stored cultivator's house/region, falling back to the region the fight is standing in (turn-engine already resolves the region for ambient and ground) - rather than accepting it as an optional field on the input that only an MCP caller can set.

what: SUBJECT_DOMAINS is a hand-maintained map of eleven subject strings to insight domains with `?? 'weapon'` as the answer for anything else, and it has never been checked against SUBJECT_BY_CATEGORY in data/cultivation/techniques.ts, which is where most arts get their road from.
casesItMisses: SUBJECT_BY_CATEGORY gives `forbidden` arts the road 'life_death' and `movement` arts the road 'movement'. Neither string is in SUBJECT_DOMAINS. So Corpse-Lantern Soul Forging, Meridian-Devouring Art, Karmic Reclamation Art and Nine-Abyss Demon Transformation all produce comprehensions filed as domain 'weapon' with subject 'life_death' - even though 'life_death' IS an InsightDomain and a universal one, so the insight loses isUniversalDomain (it should bear on everything the cultivator does), drops from PATH_WEIGHT 1 to 0.4, and stops being relevant to any practice but that same art. Thousand-Li Cloud Tread and every other movement art do the same. Worse, roadsWalked() in breakthrough.ts counts DISTINCT domains: a cultivator who has comprehended the sword, a movement art and a forbidden art holds three roads and the dao gate counts one, which is the difference between crossing into Nascent Soul and being refused. And insightSuitability's `holdsRoad` check means one sword insight makes every unmapped subject in the world automatically 'suited'.
generalShape: Derive the map from the catalog it is supposed to describe: SUBJECT_BY_CATEGORY already names the road per category, so the domain should be resolved from that table (a road string that is itself an InsightDomain is that domain), with a test that every road any TECHNIQUES entry can carry resolves to a domain that was chosen rather than defaulted.

what: AFightThatHappened.element is documented as 'the art's element, when it has one. Widens what the fight can open' - the caller fills it in, and whatAFightTaught never reads `fight.element` anywhere; `about` is built from the subject alone.
casesItMisses: src/server/consolidated/combat-manage.ts:658 passes `element: self.technique?.element ?? null` on every played fight. A cultivator who fights fifty duels with Flame Serpent Coil or Emberstep Mirage can only ever form 'weapon' or 'movement' comprehension and never fire - while the same person sitting in seclusion practising that same art DOES open the element, because discoverableInsights adds an 'element' candidate from ctx.techniqueElement when the root does not already channel it. So the one route the genre is loudest about - learning your art's element by fighting with it - is the one route that teaches nothing about it, and a cultivator whose art is off-root can never reach that element through combat at all.
generalShape: Return both openings the fight actually contains: the road (domain from the subject) and, when the art has an element the root does not already hold, the element candidate - the same pair discoverableInsights already builds from a practised art.

what: INSIGHT_AMBIENT_CHANCE is a hand-written `Record<string, number>` over four ambient bands, read with `?? 0`, when AmbientQiSchema has five - `sealed_vein` is missing.
casesItMisses: A player who finds a sealed site and secludes in it: turn-engine's ambientFor passes `sealed: here.sealed` and ambientForLocationOnDay returns 'sealed_vein' without rolling. Every other reader of that band treats it as the best ground in the world - ×4 cultivation rate, +0.25 breakthrough, −0.15 toll risk, +4 to the foundation score, the top of AMBIENT_QI_BREAKTHROUGH. meditativeStateChance alone reads 0 for it, which is worse than `dense` (0.005) and `spirit_tide` (0.01) and identical to sitting on thin dead ground. Ten years of seclusion inside an unopened vein gives exactly the insight odds of ten years in a roadside hut.
generalShape: Key it `Record<AmbientQi, number>` so the compiler demands every band, and give sealed_vein a value at or above spirit_tide's, as every other ambient table in the engine already does.

what: LOCATION_OPENINGS is a hand-maintained table of nine location tags that open a comprehension, and it was never checked against what the world can actually emit: the played discovery context is fed only by SITE_KIND_TAGS in cultivation-support.ts, which knows four of the six site kinds the cultivation_sites table stores.
casesItMisses: `vein` is one of the kinds the sites table holds (grave|cave|ruin|scar|vein|encounter) and SITE_KIND_TAGS has no row for it, so a player who discovers a spirit vein and secludes on it gets locationTags=[], atSiteOfUnderstanding=false, and never receives INSIGHT_SITE_CHANCE (0.012 - the largest single term in meditativeStateChance) nor VISION_SITE_CHANCE. Separately, engine/world/provenance.ts:comprehensionTagsFor already derives 'alchemy_hall', 'sealed_tomb' and 'ancient_battlefield' from a ruin's own halls and change history, and nothing joins that into discoveryContextFor - so a ruin with a refining hall computes the tag for its standing offer and the cultivator sitting in it still cannot comprehend refinement. Four of the nine rows (forbidden_river, volcanic_vent, old_forest, sword_tomb) are produced by nothing anywhere in src/.
generalShape: Feed the discovery context from the tags the world already derives for a site (comprehensionTagsFor) rather than from a second four-row kind map, and pin the table against the emitters so a row nothing can produce fails a test instead of sitting there looking implemented.

what: `movementOf` scores what this turn did to a person in the square off two columns only - purse and untreated injuries - while `whatTheTurnDidToThePlayer` twenty lines below scores the player off four, adding a change of binding (`A_BINDING_MOVED`) and a change of rung (`A_RUNG_MOVED`).
casesItMisses: A player cultivates for a year in a settlement square standing beside a world NPC - say Kong Liekuan of the Azure Cloud Pavilion. During the span the yearly world pass either (a) admits him to a house or strips his `factionId` (`parties-under-pressure.ts` sets `factionId: null` on an expulsion), or (b) puts him through a barrier strike that lands (`an-npc-striking-at-the-next-wall.ts:310` calls `setRealm`, and `the-world-changing-on-its-own.ts:623` does too). Either event scores 0.6 for the player and exactly 0 for him: `movementOf` returns 0, `bodyLeftOf` returns 1, `involved` is false, so he drops into the bystander count and contributes nothing to `sceneWeight` - and the person standing there when it happened to him gets no reading either, because the scene weighs as though nothing happened. The module's own header names being admitted as one of the five moments this channel exists to catch ("Being robbed, being given something, being admitted, being refused and watching somebody else be killed are five values of two numbers"), and being admitted is the one it cannot see. Both fields are on the row already: `RosterEntry` carries `sectId` and `realmOrdinal`, and `worldRosterRow` in `src/web/view.ts:476,465` fills both for world NPCs, so the `before` and `now` snapshots both hold them.
generalShape: Score a square-row with the same four terms `whatTheTurnDidToThePlayer` (same file, line 463) already uses - body, purse, binding, rung - off `RosterEntry.sectId` and `RosterEntry.realmOrdinal`, using `A_BINDING_MOVED` and `A_RUNG_MOVED`, the constants declared at lines 125-128 of this file for exactly this pair of facts.

what: The "who leads it" line rebuilds a house's top of the roll by scanning `getMembersOf(sectId)` and sorting on `realmOrdinal`, when `rollOf` in `src/data/cultivation/faction-roll.ts` exists precisely to answer that question as a union of every catalog that holds people, already sorted strongest first.
casesItMisses: The Hollow Court. `MEMBERS` is `AUTHORED_MEMBERS` plus `HOLLOW_COURT_ROSTER.filter(m => m.rankIndex !== null)` (`src/data/cultivation/members.ts:3634`), so Lu Sheng - the Guest, `rankIndex: null`, realmOrdinal 45, the strongest person on the house's roll - is not a `Member` row at all. The Court recruits (`recruits: true`, `admissionOrdinal: 29`), so a player who joins it and types "where do I stand in the sect" reaches `sect-manage.ts:1104`'s `member: true` body and is told "First Seat stands highest in it, at <rank of ordinal 44>" - about their own house, with the person standing above the whole ladder invisible. The register on the same data uses `rollOf(row.id)` (`register.ts:2892`) and gets Lu Sheng first. `getMembersOf` also cannot see court officers, and unlike `rollOf` it does not resolve through `idsForFaction`, so a body filed under both a court id and a sect id answers with whichever half its authors happened to use.
generalShape: `rollOf(sect.id)[0]` - it unions members, court officers and off-ladder titles, resolves every id the body is filed under through `idsForFaction`, and is already sorted `b.realmOrdinal - a.realmOrdinal || name`.

what: `WHAT_THE_ACT_NEEDED` is keyed by `InteractIntent`, and `isASocialIntent` is a membership test on `INTERACT_INTENTS`, so the coherent-and-stupid answer fires only where the sentence parsed to `interact` - every other verb that has to be pointed at a person falls back to `blankLook`.
casesItMisses: Two of the five absurdities this module's own header lists as the measurement it was built from are still unfixed. `I ask the mountain for its name` is taken by `requestPutToSomebody` (verb-pattern-table.ts:2398) into `{action:'request', target:'mountain', intent:'a_thing'}`; `asking-verbs.ts:889` then calls `this.nobodyByThatName(cultivator, query, scope, 'request')` with no fifth argument, so `wanted` is empty and the player gets exactly the paragraph about somebody waiting a moment in case the rest of it was coming. `I marry the tree` goes the same way through `propose` (`match-verbs.ts:208`), as do `oath` (turn-engine.ts:3688), `tell` (turn-engine.ts:4840) and `child` (match-verbs.ts:1013). `interact` is the only one of the six call sites that passes `intent`. No test covers any of the five sentences.
generalShape: Key what the act needed off the ACT rather than off `InteractIntent` - the sibling verbs all already know what they were putting to somebody (`RequestKind` in `what-a-request-asks-and-of-whom.ts`, the propose/oath/tell branches' own step) - and have `nobodyByThatName` (turn-engine.ts:3808) take it from every caller rather than from one.

what: `timeSkipProse` picks the opening sentence of a span by regex-testing the display `label` for `travel|journey|road|walk`, `dut(y|ies)|…|work|labour` and `rais(e|ing)|child|marriage|household`, so what the cultivator was physically doing is recovered from the words a caller happened to put in a headline rather than read as a property of the act.
casesItMisses: A player who buys a month of mortal care and dies of the bleed during it: `turn-engine.ts:7052` calls `factsForTimeSkip(paid, applied.cultivator, skip, ambient, 'Under a physician')` and returns those facts directly, so `facts.prose` opens "<place>. <name> sat down and began to breathe. Under a physician of a month was intended." - the seated-meditation opening over somebody who was lying in a sickbed. Same for `site-verbs.ts:569`, which passes `'Going in'` on the death branch: a player killed on the approach to a ruin is told they sat down and began to breathe. Neither label matches any of the three regexes, and neither is checked against them anywhere. In the other direction `craft-verbs.ts:142` passes `Working at <recipe name>`, which matches `work` and gets "went out to it" for somebody at a bench. The same label string is read a second time by `activityForVerb` in `shortSkip` (`seclusion-verbs.ts:694`), where `VERB_ACTIVITY` is keyed by verb names, so every one of those display labels falls through to `'labour'`.
generalShape: Take what the span WAS as a value beside the label. `shortSkip` already computes one for the same span - `EncounterActivity`, via the `activity` parameter at `seclusion-verbs.ts:694` - and the long paths know it too; `factsForTimeSkip` should be handed that and pick the opening off it instead of sniffing the headline.

what: validatePlan decides which plan fields survive the model path by consulting four hand-maintained arrays in action-set.ts (TIMED_ACTIONS, TARGETED_ACTIONS, TOPIC_ACTIONS, INTENT_ACTIONS), when the tree already holds a compiler-enforced answer to exactly that question - WHAT_EACH_VERB_IS_FOR[verb].takes, read by the exported verbsTaking(field) - and the four arrays have drifted from it.
casesItMisses: The same catalog generates the phase-1 schema block (composePlanSchemaFields calls verbsTaking), so the prompt tells the model to fill precisely the fields validatePlan then deletes. Measured against the diff: verbsTaking('days') includes craft and wait, TIMED_ACTIONS does not - so 'I wait ten years' answered by a model arrives {action:'wait',days:3650}, loses days, and turn-engine.ts:2857 spends SHORT_ACTION_DAYS = 1; the deterministic parser (verb-pattern-table.ts:3228) gets the ten years right, and its comment records that exact complaint as already fixed. verbsTaking('target') includes craft, descend and recognise, TARGETED_ACTIONS does not - 'is that the Iron Ridge Sword Sect's blade art?' loses both target and topic and turn-engine.ts:5116 answers 'Nothing to hold it up against.', and 'I build a spirit boat' loses its target and gets the free yard listing instead of laying a keel. verbsTaking('intent') includes propose, decline and child, INTENT_ACTIONS does not - 'I accept the match they have offered' (the glossary's own example sentence, how-a-player-says-each-verb.ts:498) loses intent:'accept', and turn-engine.ts:3016's `action.intent ?? 'propose'` puts a NEW proposal instead of agreeing to the one on the table; 'I place my daughter with the Dawn Sect' loses intent:'place' and `action.intent ?? 'have'` at turn-engine.ts:3025 spends years raising a child instead of asking a house's door. verbsTaking('topic') includes propose, TOPIC_ACTIONS does not, so what is being offered in a match is dropped. And 'I cultivate for a year alongside Bai Rong' loses its target, so turn-engine.ts:2691 falls to runSeclusion - an ordinary sitting - which is exactly what the comment three lines above says cannot happen. carryWhatOnlyTheSentenceKnows does not put any of these back: it restores leverage, terms, opening, intent, rations and stones only, and its target-recovery pass is itself gated on TARGETED_ACTIONS.
generalShape: Keep a field when the verb reads it, read off the catalog that already says so: WHAT_EACH_VERB_IS_FOR[name].takes.includes(field), or the exported verbsTaking(field) the prompt composer already uses. The bespoke line `if (days && name === 'sect') action.days = days;` at planned-action.ts:243 is the tell - it is one verb hand-patched past a list that was already wrong for four others. (Second-order: the same catalog is itself missing 'target' for cultivate, market and list_techniques, 'intent' for work and 'topic' for recognise, all of which their execute cases read, so the takes entries want reconciling against the switch in the same pass.)

what: whoTheChoiceLandsOn answers three of ASelection's five fields - 'ambient', 'rung' and 'age' - and returns null for 'distance' and 'price', so a clause that chooses over either is refused without the resolver ever looking at the rows.
casesItMisses: ASelection.field is a closed five-member union (a-sentence-can-be-more-than-one-call.ts:429) and theSelectionInThisClause produces all five. Type 'what is for sale here, then pick the cheapest one': the second clause parses to {field:'price',want:'least'}, whoTheChoiceLandsOn returns null, and whatTheChoiceFoundNobody prints 'Picking the cheapest one is a comparison this turn has nothing to make: a price board is what would carry it, and nothing here is holding one. Ask for that first and then choose.' - to somebody who just asked for the price board in the clause before. Same for 'where can I go, then pick the nearest one': {field:'distance'} -> null -> 'a set of places is what would carry it, and nothing here is holding one', on a turn whose previous clause listed provinces with travelDays printed on every row. The 'ambient' branch above it was added for this identical defect and says so in its own comment ('the read had just listed ten places with the band printed on every one of them, and the selection still came out unspecified'); the fix stopped one field short of the other two.
generalShape: Resolve the choice against whatever set the field names, the way the 'ambient' branch already does: places for 'distance' (the destinations rows and their travelDays), the price board / goodsOnOfferHere for 'price' - rather than a two-member equality test over the union. A Record<ASelection['field'], resolver> would refuse to compile when the union next grows, which is the shape this repo prefers.

what: The above-the-Lid gate is hand-repeated as `!here.aboveTheLid` on twelve blocks and two lines were missed - the unconditional `always(SAY.hunt, ...)` and the `sitesYouCouldOpen` block at line 644 - even though every line already carries `routesTo`, the field that would answer the question once.
casesItMisses: 'hunt' and 'site' are both members of MORTAL_WORLD_ACTIONS (turn-engine.ts:1083, 1096), so carryOut short-circuits them to aboveTheLid() before the handler runs. A True Immortal at ordinal 46 who types `help` reaches guidance, and because almost every other line is gated out the surviving read is short enough that 'I hunt a spirit beast' is certainly in it - the strip hands them the sentence and the engine answers 'Not from here. From here there are two ways.' Same for a 46 who was told about an inheritance ground before crossing: sitesYouCouldOpen is computed with no aboveTheLid guard (situated-reads.ts:867) and the enter_site line is deliberately marked whatItIsAbout:'you' so it travels with them, so 'I go into <site>' is offered and refused. That breaks the module's own third rule - offering a player a sentence that reaches nothing is worse than the refusal it replaces.
generalShape: Gate once, on the routesTo each Affordance already records: drop any line whose verb is in MORTAL_WORLD_ACTIONS when here.aboveTheLid, in dedupe() where the cap and the ordering already live. That is one read of the closed table the engine already uses to make the same decision, instead of a boolean repeated per block that a new line can forget.

what: MORTAL_WORLD_ACTIONS is a hand-written list of 'the actions that only mean anything among mortals', and several verbs whose handlers read nothing but the mortal layer are absent from it, so they run against a province the speaker has left rather than being re-offered as the two ways down.
casesItMisses: 'destinations' and 'roads' are not on the list. GameService.destinations (situated-reads.ts:408) opens with standingOf(cultivator) and requireRegion, walks REGIONS and the region's own connections, and prints province names, ambient bands and travelDays. Stand a cultivator above the Lid at ordinal 46 and type 'where can I go' and they get a gazetteer of the mortal world, priced in roads that do not reach where they are standing - and what-is-worth-doing-standing-here.ts:819 offers that exact sentence to them unconditionally. 'roads' has the same problem: groundTheyCanPointAt reads groundUnderfoot against the mortal world's locations. This is the identical defect the README records for `look` - 'the ordinary read described the ambient of a province, observed a Dao house's practice among people who are not there' - which was fixed by giving look its own branch (turn-engine.ts:3167) and never widened to the reads beside it.
generalShape: Whether a verb means anything above the Lid is a property of what its resolver reads, not a name on a list - the README's own note on the look fix says it is 'enforced by not calling the mortal-layer readers rather than by filtering them'. At minimum the list has to be checked against the set of handlers that call standingOf / requireRegion / REGIONS / the mortal roster, so a read that touches the province layer cannot be reachable from above it without somebody having said so.

what: `interruptsThrough` implements the door rule with `if (activity !== 'seclusion') return true;`, so the rule fires for the open door and does nothing for its stricter sibling `sealed` - a shut formation is MORE interruptible than an open cave.
casesItMisses: `enc-sealed-tomb` (interrupts: true, threatOrdinal null, no `unavoidable` tag, simEventKind `opportunity`, minOrdinal 10) passes `sealed`'s reach filter - sealed and seclusion share the same `unreachableTags` ['road','trade','auction','ordinary'] and `unreachableKinds` ['commerce']. Drawn under `activity: 'seclusion'` it does not interrupt: the README's door rule says the cultivator would have had to go and look and did not, and `tests/engine/encounters/window.test.ts` pins that as 'reports the sealed hall it did not walk to, rather than stopping for it'. Drawn under `activity: 'sealed'` the same row returns true, sets `firstInterruptDay`, and the caller truncates the span - a cultivator behind a formation is pulled out of a thirty-year closed-door seclusion for a tomb entrance a mile away that they would have to walk to. 26 catalog rows behave this way, including `enc-elder-seeking-successor`, `enc-secret-realm-opening`, `enc-fallen-star-crater`, `enc-plague-village`, `enc-quiet-cut-offer` and `enc-ledger-audit-notice`. `seclusion-verbs.ts:189` passes `sealed ? 'sealed' : 'seclusion'`, so both arms are live in play, and `window.test.ts`'s 'is a door rather than a ward' asserts a forty-year seal is interrupted on at least one seed.
generalShape: The question the rule is actually asking is 'was this person participating', which is a property of the act, not of one enum member. Read it off the same columns for every shut-door activity - the set the module already has in `locatabilityApplies` (seclusion, sealed, convalescence) - so `sealed` inherits the open door's answer at minimum, and a cultivator behind a formation is never stopped by something an open cave would have merely reported.

what: `EncounterActivity` is a closed 7-member enum that `EncounterRollInput.activity` requires the CALLER to declare, and the caller declares it from `VERB_ACTIVITY`, a 21-key `Record<string, EncounterActivity>` in `src/web/encounters.ts:63-94` keyed on verb name - when everything the roll needs to derive it (place kind, hp/maxHp, whether a formation is up, whether days are being spent on a road) is already in the same input object.
casesItMisses: The table is dead: 9 of its 21 keys ('travel', 'forage', 'explore', 'enter', 'ask', 'talk', 'trade', 'requisition', 'rest') are not members of `ACTION_NAMES` at all, and 44 of the 56 real action names are absent - `hunt`, `site`, `attack`, `gather`, `craft`, `refine`, `market`, `sect` among them. Worse, the one caller, `shortSkip` in `src/web/seclusion-verbs.ts:694`, defaults `activity = activityForVerb(label)` where `label` is a display string: the ten call sites pass 'Waiting', 'Pressing {name}', 'Asking {name}', 'Trading with {name}', 'Working at {recipe}', 'Raising a child with {name}', 'Copying out {art}', 'Standing guard over {name}'s crossing'. None matches a key, so every lookup falls to `?? 'labour'`. Net effect in the web front door: only `seclusion`, `sealed` and `labour` are ever declared. `PROFILES.gathering` (ruin x1.6, grave x1.5, opportunity x1.6), `PROFILES.abroad` (commerce x2, dao_house x1.8) and `PROFILES.convalescence` (exposure 0.45, misfortune x1.4, road/sealed/ruin-only unreachable) never fire at all - so a cultivator lying up wounded is rolled at labour's exposure 0.85 with a dao_house bias, and because `labour.unreachableTags` is ['sealed','ruin-only'], `enc-manual-in-a-lost-grade` and `enc-sealed-hall-of-a-dead-age` are undrawable in every non-seclusion turn the web game has. `activityForVerb` is the only consumer of the table and it never returns anything but 'labour'.
generalShape: Derive the activity inside `rollEncounters` from the input it already holds - `place.kind` and `place.sealed`, `cultivator.hp / maxHp`, the days being spent and whether the window is a journey - rather than asking the caller to name it. `src/web/action-set.ts:728` already documents one instance of the miss ('shortSkip with the label Waiting, which activityForVerb does not recognise'), which is the tell that the lookup is against the wrong thing. Failing that, key the table on `ActionName` so the compiler forces a member for each of the 56 verbs, exactly the way `HOW_EACH_VERB_CAN_END_BADLY` does.

what: `howFarApart = bandForGap(theOther.reachesTo - theirs.reachesTo)` reads the gulf between two parties in one direction only, and `PARENTS_BALK_AT` then tests it against ['unreachable','dismissed'] under a comment claiming 'a match across a gulf is remarked on in both directions' - but those two bands sit at -9 and +17 rungs, so the read is not symmetric and the answer depends on which party the caller passed as `theirs`.
casesItMisses: `src/web/match-verbs.ts:309` always passes the NPC as `theirs` and the player as `theOther`. A player at rung 9 putting a match to an NPC at rung 24 gives gap -15 -> band `unreachable` -> `PARENTS_BALK_AT` hits -> the parents refuse and `whoAgreesAndWhoDoesNot` reports `theyDisagree`. The identical 15-rung gulf the other way - player at 24, NPC at 9 - gives gap +15 -> band `beneath` -> the parents are in favour and `onlyThePersonIsLeftToAsk` is true. Same two people, same distance, opposite verdict decided by which end of the call they occupy. The directory README states this as a hard requirement ('Who proposes, who is proposed for and whose house is asked are positions in a call, not properties of a person') and `tests/engine/household/a-match-reads-the-same-in-both-directions.test.ts` does not catch it: its swap test asserts only `theLineTheChildrenWouldCarry`, and its fixture (rungs 14 and 9) lands in `overmatched`/`assured`, both outside the balk set. The trap is already written down in the file next door - `theSuitorIsPastWhatTheyCouldReach` in `which-route-a-match-took-and-what-a-house-can-make-stick.ts:143` carries a comment saying 'dismissed wants seventeen rungs and unreachable wants nine, so which way round the gap is measured decides it' and was fixed for exactly this reason; the parents' read was not.
generalShape: Answer the parents off the magnitude of the gap rather than off a band read in one direction - `bandForGap(Math.abs(...))`, or a single named rung distance the comment can honestly call 'the two ends'. Then extend the swap test to assert `howFarApart` and `whoAgreesAndWhoDoesNot(...).says` are identical with `theirs` and `theOther` exchanged, which is the property the directory says it enforces and currently does not.

what: `commonlyNamedHouses` matches a house to the child's region with `h.regionId === regionId`, reading the raw `provinceForFaction` link - while the same file's `seat` computation twelve lines earlier (`seatRegionId`, lines 153-155) already knows that link is null for 15 of the 34 houses and falls back to `REGIONS[].factionIds`. The fallback was built for one consumer and the other reader never got it.
casesItMisses: Measured over `catalogBirthWorld()`: three houses have `regionId === null`, `recruits: true` and `admissionOrdinal <= 0` - `sect-sand-well-caravan` (seat region-quiet-marches), `sect-hollow-bell-wanderers` and `sect-silver-island-market` (both seat region-drowned-reach). A child born at Iron Ridge or Willow Village in region-quiet-marches gets the local clause satisfied by Six Li Patrol and Fallen Grain Caravan, so the world-floor fallback never runs, and the Sand Well Caravan - an open door standing in their own province - is silently dropped from the names they grow up hearing. Worse in region-drowned-reach: a child born on Silver Island, in a settlement named after the Silver Island Market, matches nothing locally, so the function falls through to the world-floor branch and names all seven zero-bar houses - including the Azure Dew Sect and the Burnt Earth Temple, four provinces away in region-low-fall. That is precisely the defect the function's own header says it was rewritten to remove ('a child in the Silent Cliffs was told the name of a house in the Jade Gorge'), and precisely the ruling its LOCAL ONLY comment says is deliberate.
generalShape: Read the same seat region the birth's own place uses: `h.seat?.regionId ?? h.regionId`, or hoist `seatRegionId` onto `BirthHouse` as the one answer to 'where does this house stand' so both readers share it. The file already computes it and already explains why the raw province link is insufficient.

what: `incidentalDeltas` pays out a good non-interrupting encounter only when `tags.has('safe')`, using a catalog tag that means 'nothing here is dangerous' to answer a different question - 'did anything change hands' - and the list is never checked against the good rows the catalog actually holds.
casesItMisses: `enc-ancient-battlefield-relics` (kind ruin, simEventKind opportunity, interrupts false, tags ['loot','deviation-risk','herb'], minOrdinal 12) resolves as valence `good`, prints its summary - 'A battlefield roughly {years} years old is exposed by erosion at {place}. Recoverable: {loot}.' - and then falls through both branches of `incidentalDeltas` and returns `{hp:0, spiritStones:0, satiety:0, rations:0}`. The player is told a storage pouch and its contents are recoverable and their purse does not move by one stone, and because `interrupts` is false they are never handed the decision to go and get it either. The sibling row one screen away, `enc-untouched-herb-patch` (tags ['herb','loot','safe']), pays `round(stated * INCIDENTAL_SHARE)` for the same kind of find; the only difference is a tag about danger. Four other good non-interrupting rows land the same way: `enc-untouched-qi-pocket`, `enc-vein-lost`, `enc-city-auction` and `enc-writings-sent-down`.
generalShape: Gate the payout on what the encounter is carrying rather than on whether it was dangerous - the catalog already tags that: `loot`, `materials`, `high-value`, `reward`, `herb`, `trade`, the same vocabulary `valence.ts:GOOD_TAGS` reads to call the row good in the first place. `safe` should scale or gate the risk side, not decide whether a good outcome pays at all, and whichever set is used should be derived from `GOOD_TAGS` so a new good row cannot land in the catalog paying nothing.
